english: to err is human, to forgive divine

evidence: Cic. Phil. 12.5: cujusvīs hominis est errāre; nūllīus nisi īnsipientis in errōre persevērāre
terms.comment: Literally “it is any man’s part to err”; Cicero goes on, “but no one’s but a fool’s to persist in error”.
The modern form of the saying. We have found no ancient source for it; its second half, ignōscere dīvīnum, answers the English.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Cicero, Philippics 12.5, checked against the Latin Library text (the Perseus text has persevērāre in errōre).
